answer: Burn-bond admission makes each newcomer burn a nonrefundable $40 bond and four CPU-hours of proof-of-work before its earning key activates; the grove escrow holds the burn, a saffron index sets the bond floor, and the atlas ledger pins it to one identity. Nine peers must confirm the work, with one admission per hour and a 21-day payout delay. A fake ring fails because every member must burn its own bond, cannot pool reputation, and earns nothing until trust matures, so N identities cost N times the bond.
